rules.trigger_condition: Disruption to a critical operation that exceeds Board-approved tolerance levels (maximum outage duration, data loss tolerance, or minimum service level).
apra_reporting_content: Nature of the disruption
Action taken to address the disruption
Likely impact on business operations, depositors, policyholders, or customers
Timeframe for returning to normal operations
rules.interaction_notes: Fastest statutory reporting deadline in APRA regulations. Does NOT get waived if cyber-related; must report to APRA within 24 hours of exceeding tolerance.

rules.trigger_condition: Information security or cyber incident that materially affected, or had the potential to materially affect, the entity or customer interests (financially or non-financially), OR incident that has been notified to other regulators (OAIC, ASIC, ACSC, overseas regulators).
apra_reporting_content: Description of incident, root cause, and impacted information assets
Assessment of impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability
Remediation and containment steps undertaken
Details of other regulators notified
rules.interaction_notes: De-duplication rule: If an information security incident is reported to APRA under CPS 234 paragraph 35, CPS 230 Footnote 11 confirms it does NOT need to be separately reported under CPS 230 paragraph 33.

rules.trigger_condition: Operational risk incident (non-cyber or broad operational failure) determined likely to have a material financial impact or material impact on the ability to maintain critical operations.
apra_reporting_content: Root causes and description of operational failure
Financial impact assessment
Impact on critical operations
Remediation roadmap and control adjustments
rules.interaction_notes: Covers operational failures (fraud, system crash, process breakdown, third-party failure). If purely an info sec incident reported under CPS 234, separate reporting here is exempt per Footnote 11.

rules.trigger_condition: Material information security control weakness identified (e.g., via testing, internal audit, or penetration test) that the entity expects cannot be remediated in a timely manner.
apra_reporting_content: Details of the control gap or vulnerability
Assets and systems exposed
Reason timely remediation is not feasible
Compensating controls and revised remediation plan
rules.interaction_notes: Applies when vulnerabilities or audit findings cannot be closed within standard SLAs.

rules.trigger_condition: Entering into or materially changing an agreement for the provision of a service on which the entity relies to undertake a critical operation.
apra_reporting_content: Details of service provider and services provided
Critical operation supported
Summary of due diligence and contract compliance with CPS 230 para 58
rules.interaction_notes: Post-execution notification for critical operation agreements.

rules.trigger_condition: Prior to entering into any material offshoring arrangement, or when there is a significant change proposed (including where data or personnel relevant to the service will be located offshore).
apra_reporting_content: Jurisdiction and geographic location of provider, sub-contractors, and data
Assessment of jurisdictional legal/political risk and cloud sovereignty
Business continuity, disaster recovery, and exit arrangements
rules.interaction_notes: Must occur BEFORE signing or executing the offshoring arrangement or moving data outside Australia.

rules.trigger_condition: Annual submission to APRA of the entity's complete register of material service providers.
apra_reporting_content: Comprehensive inventory of all material service providers
Associated critical operations supported
Key fourth-party dependencies
Risk ratings and contract expiry dates
